api.why: The simplest way: nothing is installed in your store. The service reads orders and refunds through the WooCommerce REST API with a read-only key.
api.step_open: In the WordPress admin open WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API and click "Add key".
api.step_permissions: Description "Business Watchdog", user — a store administrator or shop manager, permissions "Read". Click "Generate API key".
api.step_paste: Copy the Consumer key and Consumer secret here — WooCommerce shows them only once.
api.screenshot_alt: WooCommerce API key form with Read permission; test account redacted
api.screenshot_caption: WooCommerce-Test 11.2.0: key form. Select Read permission. Test account details are redacted.
api.requirements: Required: the store address on HTTPS and permalinks other than "Plain" (Settings → Permalinks).
api.key_hint: The key starts with ck_ followed by 40 characters.
api.secret_hint: The secret starts with cs_ followed by 40 characters.
api.access_title: What the service sees and what it cannot do
api.access_reads: Reads orders (number, status, amount, currency, payment method, payment reference, dates) and refunds.
api.access_not_read: Does not keep customers, addresses, phone numbers or products: the service does not request those fields.
api.access_scope: A "Read" key can technically read other store data too, but the service only calls orders and refunds.
api.access_no_write: Nothing in the store can be changed with such a key. The service refuses keys with write permission.
api.access_frequency: Reading: changes every 5 minutes, recent orders hourly, a full 90-day check daily; at most 60 requests at a time.
api.access_revoke: Disconnect here or delete the key in WooCommerce — the service stops reading immediately.
api.verifies_store: Connecting a working key also confirms the store — no DNS record needed.
api.late_refunds_warning: On WooCommerce older than 7.9, a refund added to an older order reaches the service up to an hour later.
api.mode_warning: Without the plugin, Stripe test and live payments cannot be told apart: with a test-mode provider such orders are not supported in this mode — the plugin is needed.
api.connected: Key access verified. Order loading has started; actual results appear above.
api.polling_note: The service polls the store itself: changes every 5 minutes.
api.webhook_intro: WooCommerce can tell us itself when orders change. It is an ordinary WooCommerce setting, nothing to install; we still read orders with the read-only key.
api.webhook_none: Changes are read every 5 minutes. WooCommerce webhooks bring this down to a few seconds.
api.webhook_waiting: The secret is ready. Create the webhooks in WooCommerce and press «Check set-up» — or just save a webhook: WooCommerce sends a test request right away.
api.webhook_step_open: In WooCommerce open WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → Webhooks → Add webhook.
api.webhook_step_fields: Create one webhook per event: {topics}. Status Active, Delivery URL and Secret from the fields below, API version WP REST API Integration v3.
api.webhook_step_save: Save. If a webhook stops working nothing is lost — polling every 5 minutes stays.
api.webhook_step_check: Come back here: WooCommerce's test request shows up by itself, and «Check set-up» shows whether all webhooks are found.
api.webhook_working: Working: a signed {topic} event from WooCommerce arrived {time}.
api.webhook_rejected: A {topic} event from WooCommerce arrived {time}, but the signature did not match: the webhook has a different Secret. Paste the current secret into all four webhooks — if you did not keep it, create a new one.
api.webhook_reached: The webhooks were found in WooCommerce and are active.
api.webhook_reached_ping: WooCommerce delivered the test request of webhook #{id} ({time}) — the address is reachable and the webhook is active.
api.webhook_sign_test: One step left to check the signature: open any order in WooCommerce and press Update without changing anything. The result appears here within a minute.
api.webhook_ping_unverified: A test request of webhook #{id} arrived ({time}); comparing it with the store's webhooks…
api.webhook_not_readable: The webhook list could not be read with the key — check the set-up in WooCommerce yourself; the first signed event will confirm it.

webhook_topic.disabled: disabled by WooCommerce after failed deliveries — turn it on again (Status: Active)
webhook_topic.missing: not found — create a webhook with the address from the cabinet

webhook_issue.old_address: Some webhooks point to an old service address (from an earlier connection) — delete them.
webhook_issue.secret_newer_than_webhooks: The secret was created after the webhooks were last saved, so WooCommerce most likely has the previous one. Paste the current secret into all webhooks or create a new one.

api.webhook_waiting_issues: The webhooks were found, but there are issues — fix them as listed below and press «Check set-up».
api.webhook_effect: Nothing is lost without webhooks: orders are still read every 5 minutes. No new orders means no events — that is not an error.
api.webhook_screenshot_alt: WooCommerce webhook form: Status Active, topic, Delivery URL, Secret and API version v3
api.webhook_screenshot_caption: WooCommerce-Test 11.2.0: the webhook form. The Delivery URL and Secret are hidden in the screenshot — take them from the fields below.
api.webhook_secret_once: The secret is shown once. A new secret cancels the old one — then replace it in every webhook.
api.polling_note_with_webhook: Changes arrive at once through WooCommerce webhooks; every 5 minutes we also check everything ourselves.
api.key_rejected: The store no longer accepts the key (it was deleted or its permissions changed). Reading has stopped — create a new "Read" key, disconnect the old one and connect the new one.
api.revoke_warning: The service deletes the key on its side and stops reading orders. Delete the key in WooCommerce too (Settings → Advanced → REST API).
api.plugin_active: Orders currently come through the plugin. A store has one order source: to switch to a REST API key, first disconnect the plugin in the "{block}" section below.

shopware.why: Nothing has to be installed in your shop: the service reads Shopware 6.6 and 6.7 orders through the Admin API with an integration key. The app is optional, for instant updates and checkout observation.
shopware.step_role: In Shopware 6.7 open Settings → Users & permissions → Roles and create a role "Business Watchdog" with a single permission: Orders → View.
shopware.roles_screenshot_alt: Roles area in Shopware-Test settings, with no buyer data
shopware.roles_screenshot_caption: Shopware-Test 6.7.15.1: Settings → Users & permissions → Create role.
shopware.role_form_screenshot_alt: Shopware role form with View, Edit, Create, Delete and All permission columns
shopware.role_form_screenshot_caption: Enter the role name. The first permission column is View.
shopware.permission_screenshot_alt: Shopware role permission grid with Orders and View column
shopware.permission_screenshot_caption: For the new role, select only View for Orders. Leave other rights off.
shopware.integration_screenshot_alt: Shopware integration form with key and secret redacted
shopware.integration_screenshot_caption: Settings → Integrations → Add integration. Leave Administrator off, select the role and copy the keys before saving. Keys are redacted here.
shopware.step_integration: Open Settings → Integrations → Add integration: name "Business Watchdog", "Administrator" off, assign the new role. Save.
shopware.step_paste: Copy the Access key ID and Secret access key here — Shopware shows the secret only once.
shopware.requirements: Required: the store address on HTTPS where the Admin API (/api) is reachable.
shopware.access_reads: Reads orders: number, status, amount, currency, payment method, payment status and PayPal payment reference.
shopware.access_not_read: Does not request customers, addresses or products — the service limits the response fields explicitly.
shopware.access_calls: Sends only the token request and order searches; nothing is changed in the store.
shopware.state_risk: Important: in Shopware 6.6 and 6.7 even a key with a "view only" role can technically change order, payment and delivery statuses (a Shopware limitation, reported to the developers). It cannot move money or edit orders. The service never sends such requests and keeps the key encrypted. Keep the key secret.
shopware.acknowledge: I understand: the key can change statuses; the service only uses it for reading
shopware.state_risk_short: The key can technically change order statuses — keep it secret; the service only reads.
shopware.refunds_note: Shopware records a refund only as the payment status: for a partial refund the amount is shown from the payment provider (PayPal), and the check against the store is "no data".
shopware.connected: Shopware access verified. Order loading has started; actual results appear above.
shopware.key_rejected: Shopware no longer accepts the key (the integration was deleted or its role changed). Reading has stopped — create a new integration and connect it.
shopware.revoke_warning: The service deletes the key on its side and stops reading orders. Delete the integration in Shopware too (Settings → System → Integrations).
shopware.method_app_hint: On top of the key: changes arrive at once and you see whether real shoppers can complete checkout. Requires installing the app in Shopware.
shopware.method_key_hint: Nothing installed in the shop: create a read-only role and an integration in Shopware and paste the key. Changes are read every 5 minutes.
shopware.app_step_download: Save the downloaded BusinessWatchdog.zip. Do not unpack it.
shopware.app_step_upload: In the Shopware admin open Extensions → My extensions → Upload extension and choose BusinessWatchdog.zip.
shopware.app_step_install: Find Business Watchdog in the extension list, click Install, then Activate and approve the permissions.
shopware.app_permissions: The app asks only to read orders, payments, currencies and payment methods. Nothing is read until you confirm the store with a code.
shopware.app_step_open: In Shopware open Extensions → My extensions, click «…» next to Business Watchdog and choose «Open extension».
shopware.app_step_code: Copy the code below, paste it on the app page and confirm. The shop address must match this store’s address in your account.
shopware.app_code_hint: The code is valid until {time} and only for this store.
shopware.app_code_waiting: Waiting for the code to be entered in the app; this page updates by itself.
shopware.app_downloaded: App file downloaded. Upload it in Shopware.
shopware.app_waiting: Waiting for the app to be installed in Shopware.
shopware.app_not_active_yet: The app has registered but is not activated yet — click Activate in Shopware.
shopware.app_auto_refresh: The status updates by itself once the app is activated.
shopware.app_realtime_note: New orders and payment status changes arrive right away; every 5 minutes the service also checks for changes.
shopware.app_revoke_warning: The service stops reading orders. Remove the app in Shopware too (Extensions → My extensions).
shopware.app_version_note: Because of its own bug, Shopware 6.6.10.25–6.6.10.29 cannot install apps that connect to a server — on those versions choose "Integration key". The app works on 6.7 and on 6.6 up to 6.6.10.24.
shopware.app_test_download_note: Local environment: you can download the current app version {version} at any time to try it on your Shopware shop.
shopware.stripe_note: Money checks for Shopware cover PayPal (SwagPayPal) and Stripe (the "Stripe Payment" plugin). Orders paid through other Stripe apps or other providers are shown as "payment method not supported" — no false discrepancies. The Stripe plugin does not carry refunds into Shopware: a refund made in Stripe is shown as information.
shopware.app_step_cache: Clear the Shopware cache (Settings → System → Caches & indexes → Clear cache) so that checkout observation starts on the checkout page.
shopware.app_script_note: The app also adds a small observation script to the order confirmation and «Thank you» pages. It only counts checkout stages (page shown, order sent, order placed), uses no cookies and reads no shopper data. The shopper's browser sends the counts only to your shop; Business Watchdog collects them from there. It works when the browser check signs in as a test customer or a guest.
shopware.app_version_unknown: unknown (shown after the first event from Shopware)
shopware.app_update_step_download: Download the update file (button below) — it is made for this same connection, nothing has to be connected again.
shopware.app_update_step_confirm: Shopware sees the app is installed — click «Update».
shopware.app_update_downloaded: Update file downloaded. Upload it in Shopware.
shopware.service_url_hint: The service URL is for reference and is already built into the app. Enter only the connection code in Shopware.

advice.MONEY_UNSUPPORTED: The order's payment method is not supported by reconciliation. Check the payment manually in the provider dashboard.
advice.MONEY_CAPTURE_MISSING: Find the transaction in the provider dashboard and check the order status. If the payment went through under another reference, match it manually. Not finding a capture does not prove the money is missing.
advice.MONEY_CAPTURE_AMOUNT: Compare the order total with the provider capture: a partial capture, an order change or a gateway error are possible.
advice.MONEY_CAPTURE_NOT_RECORDED: Check the order and payment gateway log. The provider confirmed the capture; restore the order state without charging again.
advice.MONEY_REFUND_MISSING: Check whether the refund was actually sent through the provider and not only marked in the store.
advice.MONEY_REFUND_EXTRA: Check who issued the refund in the provider dashboard and whether the order should reflect it.
advice.MONEY_MULTIPLE_CAPTURES: Check whether the customer was charged twice. Refund if necessary.
advice.MONEY_CURRENCY_MISMATCH: Check the currency settings of the store and the payment gateway.
advice.MONEY_ORDER_CHANGED: The order was edited after payment. Make sure the final total and the capture agree.
advice.MONEY_PAYMENT_WITHOUT_ORDER: Find the payment in the provider dashboard and work out which order it belongs to. A match by amount and time is only a hint.
advice.MONEY_PAYMENT_NOT_MATCHED: No provider payment was found for the order's reference — this does not prove the money is missing. Check how the order was paid and who marked it paid; if the payment exists under another reference, link it manually.
advice.MONEY_CANCELLED_PAID: The cancelled status alone does not return money. Check whether the customer needs a refund and issue it through the payment provider.
advice.MONEY_PAYMENT_FAILED_ORDER_OPEN: The provider refused the payment and no money arrived, yet the store still waits for it. Do not ship the order: cancel it or ask the buyer to pay again.
advice.CHECKOUT_PAYMENTS_FAILING: Try paying with this method yourself and check the payment plugin log and the provider dashboard.
advice.CHECKOUT_FLOW_FAILED: Open the site and walk the path to payment: product, cart, checkout. Look at the check screenshot. This check does not verify that charging succeeds.
advice.CHECKOUT_TEST_PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE: Make sure the test product is published, in stock and can be added to the cart.
advice.CHECKOUT_MONITORING_BLOCKED: Site protection (WAF, CAPTCHA) or a site dialog the check could not close blocks the check. This is not a store failure, but the store cannot be checked right now.
advice.CHECKOUT_ADAPTER_UNSUPPORTED: The theme or checkout plugins are not supported yet. This is not a store failure; we cannot check this path.
advice.INTEGRATION_STALE: Check that the site is up and the Business Watchdog plugin is active. This does not mean sales stopped, but while the plugin is silent the service cannot see orders.
advice.INTEGRATION_DELIVERY_DELAYED: The plugin is behind with sending data. Check that scheduled tasks run on the site (WP-Cron or Action Scheduler).
advice.unknown: Open the details below and check the affected part of the store.
advice.CHECKOUT_TEST_ACCOUNT_REJECTED: Check that the test customer account exists in the shop and is active, and update the e-mail and password in the check settings. This is not a shop failure; until signing in works, payment methods are not checked.
advice.CHECKOUT_SCRIPT_SILENT: The checkout page is shown, but the observation script is silent. Check the browser console on the checkout page, that the Business Watchdog plugin or app is active and that optimisation plugins or the CSP do not block it. This does not prove that customers cannot pay.
advice.CHECKOUT_SUBMIT_FAILING: Place a test order to the end and look at errors on the page and in the logs of the shop and its payment plugins: «Submit order» is sent, but no new orders and no «Thank you» page follow.
advice.DISPUTE_OPEN: Open the dispute in the payment provider's dashboard, check the order and submit evidence (invoice, proof of delivery, correspondence) before the deadline. While the dispute is open, do not refund separately — that can cost the amount twice.
advice.DISPUTE_INQUIRY: Answer the inquiry in the payment provider's dashboard before the deadline — otherwise the bank may open a dispute. While it is open, avoid a separate refund unless needed.

cause.provider_data_incomplete: the provider data is not complete — the capture may appear after loading
cause.store_marked_failed_after_payment: the store marked the payment failed or cancelled the order after the capture
cause.notification_not_processed: the payment notification did not reach the store or was not processed by the payment module
cause.status_changed_manually: the order status was changed by hand
cause.refund_marked_only: the refund was only marked in the store and never sent through the payment system
cause.refund_failed_at_provider: the refund was sent, but the payment system declined it
cause.refund_partial_at_provider: only part of the amount was refunded at the provider
cause.step_failed_on_site: the site showed an error or did not respond at this step
cause.page_changed: the page or theme changed and the element is no longer found
cause.temporary_outage: a temporary site or network outage during the check
cause.key_revoked_or_changed: the access key was revoked, deleted or replaced
cause.site_unreachable: the site is unreachable or answers very slowly
cause.plugin_not_active: the plugin is installed but not activated or not connected

cause.plugin_disabled: the plugin was disabled or removed
cause.refund_made_at_provider: the refund was made directly in the payment system's dashboard, bypassing the store

provider.title: Payment provider
provider.subtitle: Payment provider data is needed to check that order money was really captured and refunded. Without it reconciliation shows “unknown”, not “all fine”. Connect the provider your store takes payments with.
provider.why: Connect Stripe with a read-only key. The key is entered here, not in WordPress, so money data reaches us without passing through the store.
provider.step_dashboard: In Stripe open Developers → API keys → “Create restricted key”.
provider.step_permissions: Grant Read on Payment Intents, Charges and Refunds, on Disputes to see disputes, and on Balance to see fees (optionally Account and Webhook Endpoints, so the cabinet can check the webhook set-up itself). No write permissions are needed.
provider.step_paste: Copy the key (rk_live_… or rk_test_…) and paste it below.
provider.key_hint: The key is checked for read access and stored encrypted; afterwards we only show its last 4 characters.
provider.secret_key_warning: This is a full secret key — do not enter it. Create a restricted read-only key.
provider.storage_note: Right after connecting, the store's orders of the last 90 days are reconciled again.
provider.connected: Stripe connected. The first sync runs within 15 minutes, or start it now.
provider.account_unverified: the key cannot read the account
provider.sync_incomplete: the window is finished on the next runs
provider.webhook_off: not configured — data arrives every 15 minutes
provider.polling_note: Sync runs every 15 minutes and re-reads 90 days daily; the webhook only speeds delivery up.
provider.webhook_step_add: In Stripe open Workbench → Webhooks (formerly Developers → Webhooks) → Add destination and enter the address below.
provider.webhook_step_events: Choose the events payment_intent.*, charge.* and refund.*.
provider.webhook_step_secret: Copy the Signing secret (whsec_…) and paste it here.
provider.webhook_waiting_stripe: The secret is saved; no event from Stripe yet — they come with new payments and refunds. To check right away: in Stripe open Workbench → Webhooks → this address → any event from the last 15 days → Resend.
provider.webhook_waiting_paypal: The Webhook ID is saved; no event from PayPal yet — they come with new payments, refunds and disputes. PayPal simulator events cannot be used: PayPal does not confirm their signature.
provider.webhook_rejected_stripe: An event from Stripe arrived {time}, but the signature did not match: the Signing secret saved here is not the right one. Copy the Signing secret of this address in Stripe and save it again.
provider.webhook_rejected_paypal: A {type} event from PayPal arrived {time}, but PayPal did not confirm it with the saved Webhook ID. Copy the Webhook ID of this address in the PayPal app and save it again.
provider.webhook_check_ok: A webhook with this address was found in {provider}, and the needed events are selected.
provider.webhook_check_permission: The cabinet cannot check the webhook set-up in Stripe: the key lacks Webhook Endpoints: Read (optional). The first event will confirm it.
provider.webhook_check_not_readable: The webhook set-up could not be read.

webhook_issue.endpoint_disabled: The webhook is disabled in Stripe — enable it.

provider.key_rejected: Stripe rejected the key — calls to Stripe stopped and money reconciliation shows “unknown”. Disconnect this connection and connect Stripe again with a new key.

paypal.official_docs_image: Screenshot of the official PayPal guide to finding Client ID and Secret
paypal.why: PayPal is connected with the credentials of a separate REST app in your PayPal account. They are entered here, not in WordPress, so money data reaches the service around the store.
paypal.step_app: Open developer.paypal.com → Apps & Credentials, choose Live (or Sandbox for testing) and create an app “Business Watchdog” (type Merchant).
paypal.step_features: In the app settings untick everything and enable only Transaction Search — it is needed to list payments. Optionally enable Customer disputes too (under Add-on services), to see customer disputes (it also lets the app answer disputes; the service never uses that).
paypal.step_copy: Copy the app’s Client ID and Secret and paste them below.
paypal.warning_body: Even an app with only Transaction Search may, by PayPal’s rules, refund payments and capture authorizations. Business Watchdog never does this: the service only calls read methods from a fixed list and blocks any other request before it is sent. The credentials are stored encrypted, and you can delete the app in PayPal at any time.
paypal.acknowledge: I understand: the PayPal app credentials allow more than the service needs; the service uses them for reading only.
paypal.storage_note: Right after connecting, the store’s orders of the last 90 days are reconciled again. PayPal’s payment list lags about 1–3 hours behind.
paypal.connected: PayPal is connected. The first sync runs within 15 minutes, or start it now.
paypal.rights_note: Not used by the service: reading only, from a fixed list.
paypal.search_refreshed: PayPal payment list refreshed up to {time}
paypal.webhook_off: not set up — payments arrive from the PayPal list, up to a few hours late
paypal.polling_note: Sync runs every 15 minutes over PayPal’s transaction list and re-reads 90 days once a day; a webhook reports payments and refunds right away.
paypal.webhook_step_add: In the PayPal app open Webhooks → “Add Webhook” and enter the address below.
paypal.webhook_step_events: Select the events Payment capture completed, pending, denied, refunded, reversed and Checkout order completed. To get disputes at once, add Customer dispute created, updated and resolved.
paypal.webhook_step_id: Copy the Webhook ID of the new webhook and paste it here.
paypal.revoke_warning: The PayPal credentials stop being used; money reconciliation of PayPal orders returns to “unknown”. Delete the app in PayPal as well.

observation_texts.title: Texts for your store's privacy policy
observation_texts.intro: The observation script needs no consent from shoppers and no entry in a cookie banner, but the store has to mention it in its privacy policy (Art. 13 GDPR). Below are a ready paragraph and a legitimate interest assessment (LIA) template in German and English. They are samples, not legal advice: check them and adapt them if needed.
observation_texts.lia_hint: Fill in the LIA template with your store's details and keep it with your data protection records — data protection officers often ask for it.

observation_texts.failed: The texts could not be loaded. Please try again later.

checkout_layout.not_found: The last browser check did not find the elements of this setting on the confirmation page. Observation is not confirmed; check the selectors after a theme change.
checkout_layout.title: Checkout pages and elements
checkout_layout.intro: For a Shopware store with a third-party theme or a custom checkout. The browser check and the app's observation script look for these pages and elements; an empty field means the Shopware default (shown in grey). Page paths and CSS selectors only, no JavaScript.
checkout_layout.hint: A path starts with «/» and is compared with the end of the page address, so language prefixes like /de work. If the elements are no longer found after a theme change, observation is marked «not confirmed», not «checkout broken». The address the check opens can still be set in the check settings; without it the check opens the confirmation page from here.

error.checkout_layout_path_invalid: A path starts with «/», without «..», «//», ? or # (for example /checkout/confirm).
error.checkout_layout_selector_invalid: Only letters, digits, space and # . - _ [ ] = : " ' > ~ + * , ( ) ^ $ | are allowed.
